item.title: Apple bets cheaper AI will woo small developers
item.description: As AI experimentation grows more expensive, Apple is waiving cloud API costs for developers with fewer than 2 million first-time App Store downloads.

item.title: WWDC 2026: Everything announced on Siri AI, iOS 27, Apple Intelligence and more
item.description: Apple primarily made the case for an improved experience with its longstanding Siri assistant, which like most other announcements had a hefty helping of AI.

item.title: Apple just taught your iPhone to finish your sentences, your photos, and your workflows
item.description: Apple is adding new AI-powered features to Safari, Shortcuts, and Password apps.

item.title: Apple will let you build workflows using AI in its new Shortcuts app
item.description: Shortcuts gets an AI upgrade, letting you describe the workflow you want in a prompt.

item.title: Apple’s Image Playground doesn’t suck anymore
item.description: Apple's AI image generator is getting a makeover that could make it more competitive.

item.title: Apple’s Photos app is getting new AI editing features
item.description: A new spatial "Reframe" feature will let users use AI to adjust perspectives.

item.title: Apple gives Siri its own dedicated app
item.description: Siri is finally getting its own app.

item.title: Apple is fixing the headache of splitting the bill with its new Siri in Camera feature
item.description: "If you're grabbing a bite with friends and point your iPhone at the bill, then [you can] select what you ordered to split the tab with Apple Cash," said Apple VP of Software Sebastien Marineau-Mes.

item.title: Apple’s long-awaited AI Siri overhaul is finally here
item.description: The idea behind the new "Siri AI" is to turn the assistant from a voice controlled assistant into an AI companion that can do a lot more.

item.title: Amazon now lets you design custom merch using AI
item.description: A new feature in the Amazon Shopping app allows users to generate designs with Alexa, then print them on products like T-shirts, hoodies, and tumblers.

item.title: WWDC 2026: What to expect, from Siri’s highly anticipated revamp to Apple Intelligence and iOS 27
item.description: Apple's WWDC nears: Here's what you can look forward to.

item.title: Is this the dawn of the Tokenpocalypse?
item.description: We're likely to see more price increases as the big AI companies plan to go public.

item.title: Notion restores access to Anthropic after service disruption
item.description: Notion's head of product said he was "astonished" at “the amount of people RT-ing this."

item.title: OpenAI is still working on that ‘super app’
item.description: "Chat is dead" — at least, according to a senior OpenAI employee.

item.title: OpenAI unveils Lockdown Mode to protect sensitive data from prompt injection attacks
item.description: Even with Lockdown Mode, ChatGPT could be vulnerable to prompt injections, but the goal is to reduce the likelihood that sensitive data gets shared in the process.

item.title: Sriram Krishnan is leaving his role as White House AI advisor
item.description: Krishnan is reportedly starting a new institution to continue shaping Trump's AI policy.

item.title: The Trump administration might take an equity stake in OpenAI
item.description: President Donald Trump said he's discussing deals "where the American people can benefit from the success of AI."

item.title: Startup Battlefield 200 applications officially close in 3 days
item.description: Applications for Startup Battlefield 200 officially close on June 8, 11:59 p.m. PT. Don't wait any longer. Secure your shot at competing on the Disrupt Stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 this October at San Francisco's Moscone West.

item.title: Google will pay SpaceX $920M per month for compute
item.description: In a statement, a Google representative described the deal as a result of unexpected demand for its recently launched AI products.

item.title: The most interesting startups right now want to get you off your phone
item.description: While the AI fundraising machine keeps breaking its own records, some founders are building in the other direction.  Mirror founder Brynn Putnam just raised money for Board, a startup focused on bringing people together through in-person games and social experiences. Cyberdeck creators are going viral crafting whimsical DIY computers that literally encourage users to touch grass.
